entries: Manufacturing potters prepare clay, throw and form pieces, trim, glaze, and fire ceramics in manufacturing settings. They operate equipment and control temperature curves to ensure body shape and glaze quality meet product requirements.
Prepare and condition clay, controlling moisture and plasticity.
Throw, mold, or trim pieces to ensure regular body shapes.
Apply glaze with uniform thickness to avoid crawling.
Load kilns and set and monitor firing temperature curves.
Inspect glaze color and deformation after firing and select defects for refiring.
Maintain equipment and molds and record process parameters.

paragraphs: At shift handover, first verify formulations and kiln conditions. Prepare clay, throw pieces on the wheel, trim them, and leave them to dry. Before glazing, clean the bodies, then dip or spray glaze while controlling thickness. Load and ignite the kiln and monitor its curve, sometimes rising at night to inspect the fire color. After opening the kiln, separate warped pieces and those with glaze crawling, warehouse qualified products, record parameters, and hand over the shift.

In one line: prepare, form, and fire clay into objects. The work includes clay preparation and throwing, trimming and glazing, kiln loading and temperature control, glaze inspection, and equipment maintenance. It is a craft of clay and fire requiring both hands and eyes.

This career develops tactile control and patience. The clay's moisture, wheel speed, and fire color in the kiln are learned through years of experience. It suits steady-handed people who can stay focused, enjoy the journey from clay to vessel, and tolerate workshop dust and heat.
